name: City Council Special Meeting Strategic Planning Workshop - 8:30 a.m.
agenda_text:
CITY COUNCIL OF MONTEREY PARK
  THE CITY COUNCIL ACTING ON BEHALF OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY OF THE
  FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY, THE HOUSING AUTHORITY, THE MONTEREY
  PARK FINANCING AUTHORITY AND THE MONTEREY PARK GEOLOGIC HAZARD
  ABATEMENT DISTRICT AGENDA

  SPECIAL MEETING
  Courtyard by Marriott
  Boardroom
  555 N. Atlantic Boulevard, Monterey Park

  Saturday
  April 8, 2023
  8:30 a.m.

  Note: Parking will be validated and available at no cost to attendees

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services
  to enhance the quality of life for our entire community.

GENERAL INFORMATION
Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office located
at 320 West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754, during normal business hours and the
City’s website at www.montereypark.ca.gov/AgendaCenter/City-Council-17.

The Special Meeting will not be televised on the city’s cable channel MPKTV (AT&T U-verse,
channel 99 or Charter Communications, channel 182) or on the city’s website at
http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/133/City-Council-Meeting-Videos.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
You may speak up to 5 minutes on Agenda item. You may combine up to 2 minutes of time with
another person’s speaking. No person may speak more than a total of 10 minutes. The Mayor
and City Council may change the amount of time allowed for speakers.

Per the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this
meeting, please call City Hall at (626) 307-1359 for reasonable accommodation at least 24 hours
before a meeting. Council Chambers are wheelchair accessible.

 CALL TO ORDER  Mayor
 ROLL CALL  Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong, Yvonne Yiu
   Monterey Park City Council and Successor Agency Agenda, April 8, 2023 - Page 2

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS:
Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.3(a), the public may address the City Council
only on matters listed on the Agenda. Those wishing to speak on an agenda item must utilize
one of the methods listed above. NO OTHER PUBLIC COMMENT WILL BE ACCEPTED. To
ensure the workshop begins and ends on time, the total time allocated for all public
comment, regardless of the number of speakers, is 15 minutes. If you were unable to speak
during this part of public comment, the City Council may, but is not required to, provide an
opportunity for such comment at the end of the workshop. Written communications will be
provided to the City Council but will not be read out loud.

NEW BUSINESS

 1.  STRATEGIC PLANNING WORKSHOP
  This is a City Council workshop to prioritize the City’s legislative and project agenda. It is
  anticipated that the workshop will not result in the City Council taking any particular action.
  Instead, City Councilmembers and key staff members will be reviewing the City Council’s
  previous strategic plan; updating it; and providing direction to the City Manager. Topics
  may include, without limitation, infrastructure improvements; revenue enhancement; land
  use challenges; sustainability efforts; redevelopment; community engagement and
  outreach; and municipal property needs assessment. Any direction provided by the City
  Council will appear on future meeting agendas. The anticipated outline of the workshop
  will follow this general order:
  •  Overview
  •  Benefits of Good Government
  •  Governing Body/Team Effectiveness
  •  Strategies for Creating a More Collaborative Governing Body
  •  Refresher on the Council-Manager Form of Government
  •  Review Accomplishments for 2022, Explore Plans for remainder of 2023 and into
  2024
  •  Hot Topics
  •  Strategic Plan
  •  Next Steps

ADJOURN

  MINUTES
  MONTEREY PARK CITY COUNCIL
  FINANCING AUTHORITY (MPFA)
  HOUSING AUTHORITY (MPHA)
  GEOLOGIC HAZARD ABATEMENT DISTRICT (GHAD)
  SUCCESSOR AGENCY (SA)
  SPECIAL MEETING
  APRIL 8, 2023

The City Council, the Financing Authority (MPFA), the Housing Authority (MPHA), the
Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the City
of Monterey Park held a Special Meeting of the Council in the Boardroom of the Courtyard
Marriott, 555 N. Atlantic Boulevard in the City of Monterey Park on Saturday, April 8, 2023
at 8:30 a.m.

CALL TO ORDER:
Mayor Sanchez called the meeting to order at 8:30 a.m.

ROLL CALL:
Deputy City Clerk Cindy Trang called the roll:

Council Members Present:  Henry Lo, Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong,
  Yvonne Yiu
Council Members Absent:  None

ALSO PRESENT: City Manager Ron Bow, City Attorney Karl Berger, Assistant City
Manager Inez Alvarez, City Librarian Diana Garcia, Public Works Director Shawn Igoe,
Finance Director Martha Garcia, Fire Chief Matthew Hallock, Police Chief Scott Weise,
Director of Human Resources and Risk Management Christine Tomikawa, Recreation
and Community Services Director Robert Aguirre, Interim Community Development
Director Jessica Serrano, Secretary to the City Manager Diana Wong

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS – None.

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services to enhance
  the quality of life for our entire community.
   71-87
  April 8, 2023
NEW BUSINESS

1.  STRATEGIC PLANNING WORKSHOP

  This is a City Council workshop to prioritize the City’s legislative and project agenda.
  It is anticipated that the workshop will not result in the City Council taking any
  particular action. Instead, City Councilmembers and key staff members will be
  reviewing the City Council’s previous strategic plan; updating it; and providing
  direction to the City Manager. Topics may include, without limitation, infrastructure
  improvements; revenue enhancement; land use challenges; sustainability efforts;
  redevelopment; community engagement and outreach; and municipal property
  needs assessment. Any direction provided by the City Council will appear on future
  meeting agendas. The anticipated outline of the workshop will follow this general
  order:

  •  Overview
  •  Benefits of Good Government
  •  Governing Body/Team Effectiveness
  •  Strategies for Creating a More Collaborative Governing Body
  •  Refresher on the Council-Manager Form of Government
  •  Review Accomplishments for 2022, Explore Plans for remainder of 2023
  and into 2024
  •  Hot Topics
  •  Strategic Plan
  •  Next Steps

RECESSED AND RECONVENED
The City Council recessed at 10:00 a.m. and reconvened with all council members
present at 10:15 a.m.

  DISCUSSION: City Consultant, Patrick Ibarra of the Mejorando Group, facilitated a
  strategic workshop for the City Council to discuss ideas and suggestions towards
  the future vision of the City. The City Council ensued in discussions regarding
  Benefits of Good Government; Governing Body/Team Effectiveness; Strategies for
  Creating a More Collaborative Governing Body; Refresher on the Council-Manager
  form of government; Review Accomplishments for 2022 and Explore Plans for
  remainder of 2023 and into 2024; Hot Topics including discussion on Community:
  coordinating response on next steps, mental health services, homelessness, safety;
  Economic Development: Downtown Master Plan, parking structures, Atlantic
  Square, redevelopment; Outreach: public engagement; Infrastructure: condition of
  city streets; Environmental: sustainability; Housing: affordability housing; Amenities:
  parking improvements, repair swimming pool; Strategic Plan and Next Steps to
  include periodic updates and inclusion in future council reports. City Manager Bow
  announced the appointment of Jessica Serrano as the new Community
  Development Director.
   71-88
  April 8, 2023
RECESSED AND RECONVENED
The City Council recessed at 11:50 a.m. and reconvened with all council members
present at 12:20 p.m.

  Action Taken: No reportable action taken.

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business for consideration, the meeting was adjourned at 2:46
p.m.
